rubric.why: Phagocytosis is distinguished by the type of material taken into the cell.
rubric.description: Identifies phagocytosis as uptake of solid particles.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a cell engulfs solid particles or food particles during phagocytosis.

rubric.why: Pinocytosis is distinguished by uptake of fluid and substances dissolved in it.
rubric.description: Identifies pinocytosis as uptake of liquids or dissolved substances.
rubric.how: Award for stating that a cell takes in liquid or fluid containing dissolved substances during pinocytosis.

modelAnswer: In phagocytosis, a cell engulfs solid particles to form a vesicle.
In pinocytosis, a cell takes in liquids and dissolved substances in small vesicles.

items.followUp: What are leucoplasts, and state one function of them.

rubric.why: Chromoplasts are identified by their pigments and colour.
rubric.description: Defines chromoplasts as coloured plastids containing pigments other than chlorophyll.
rubric.how: Award for identifying them as coloured plastids or mentioning their pigments.

rubric.why: Chromoplast pigments give colour to plant parts and help attract animals involved in pollination or seed dispersal.
rubric.description: States the colour-giving role and an attraction-related function.
rubric.how: Award for stating that they colour flowers/fruits and attract pollinators or animals.

modelAnswer: Chromoplasts are coloured plastids containing pigments other than chlorophyll, such as carotenoids.
They give colour to flowers and fruits, and their colours attract pollinators or animals that help disperse seeds.

items.followUp: How does cytokinesis take place in an animal cell?

rubric.why: Plant cells divide their cytoplasm by forming a cell plate rather than by pinching inward.
rubric.description: States that a cell plate forms at the equator of the cell.
rubric.how: Award for identifying cell-plate formation at the cell's equator.

rubric.why: The cell plate develops into a partition that separates the two daughter cells.
rubric.description: Explains that the cell plate grows outward and divides the cytoplasm.
rubric.how: Award for describing the plate's growth/joining with the cell boundary and the resulting division into two cells.

modelAnswer: In a plant cell, vesicles gather at the equator and fuse to form a cell plate.
The cell plate grows outward and joins the cell boundary, dividing the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.

items.followUp: What is aneuploidy, and how can it result from an error in cell division?

rubric.why: Non-disjunction is the failure of chromosomes or chromatids to separate properly.
rubric.description: Defines non-disjunction as failure of chromosome separation.
rubric.how: Award for stating that homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids fail to separate.

rubric.why: Failure to separate produces cells or gametes with an abnormal chromosome number.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that the resulting cells/gametes have extra or missing chromosomes, or an abnormal chromosome number.

modelAnswer: Non-disjunction is the failure of homologous chromosomes or sister chromatids to separate during cell division.
It produces cells or gametes with an abnormal number of chromosomes, with some having an extra or missing chromosome.

items.followUp: How does a change in pH affect an enzyme's activity?

rubric.why: Very high temperature disrupts the bonds that maintain an enzyme's three-dimensional shape.
rubric.description: Explains that high temperature disrupts bonds and changes the enzyme's shape.
rubric.how: Award for mentioning disruption of weak bonds or alteration of the enzyme's structure.

rubric.why: A changed active site prevents normal substrate binding and enzyme function.
rubric.description: Connects the changed shape to loss of substrate binding or activity.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the active site changes so the substrate cannot bind properly, or that the enzyme loses activity.

modelAnswer: At very high temperatures, weak bonds maintaining an enzyme's three-dimensional shape are disrupted, changing its shape (denaturing it).
The active site changes shape, so the substrate no longer fits and the enzyme loses its activity.

items.followUp: Differentiate between photosynthesis and respiration in terms of energy change.

rubric.why: Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler ones.
rubric.description: Describes anabolism as synthesis of complex substances from simpler substances.
rubric.how: Award for stating that anabolism builds complex molecules from simple molecules; energy use may also be mentioned.

rubric.why: Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler ones.
rubric.description: Describes catabolism as breakdown of complex substances into simpler substances.
rubric.how: Award for stating that catabolism breaks complex molecules into simple molecules; energy release may also be mentioned.

modelAnswer: Anabolism builds complex molecules from simpler molecules and usually requires energy.
Catabolism breaks complex molecules into simpler molecules and usually releases energy.

items.followUp: Explain how carbon dioxide concentration affects the rate of photosynthesis.

rubric.why: Light provides energy for photosynthesis, so increasing its intensity raises the rate up to a limit.
rubric.description: States the effect of increasing light intensity on photosynthesis.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the rate increases with light intensity until another factor limits it or the rate reaches a maximum.

rubric.why: Photosynthesis is enzyme-controlled: warming increases its rate up to an optimum, while excessive heat damages enzymes.
rubric.description: Describes the effect of temperature, including the optimum or decline at high temperature.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the rate rises to an optimum and then falls at high temperature due to enzyme denaturation.

modelAnswer: As light intensity increases, the rate of photosynthesis increases until it reaches a maximum or another factor becomes limiting.
As temperature rises, the rate increases up to an optimum; above it, the rate falls because photosynthetic enzymes denature.

items.followUp: Define tissue and explain the tissue level of organization with an example.

rubric.why: An organ is formed by different tissues working together to perform a particular function.
rubric.description: Defines an organ as different tissues working together for a specific function.
rubric.how: Award for identifying the combination of tissues and their coordinated specific function.

rubric.why: An organ system consists of multiple organs working together.
rubric.description: Defines an organ system as a group of organs working together.
rubric.how: Award for stating that an organ system comprises multiple organs that work together.

rubric.why: The coordinated organs of a system carry out a major body function.
rubric.description: Explains the purpose of the organ-system level.
rubric.how: Award for stating that the system's organs collectively perform a major function.

rubric.why: A suitable example demonstrates the organ-system level of organization.
rubric.how: Award for a valid example such as the digestive, respiratory, or circulatory system.

modelAnswer: An organ is a body part made of different tissues working together to perform a specific function.
At the organ-system level, a group of organs works together to carry out a major function of the body.
For example, the digestive system includes organs such as the stomach and intestines, which work together in digestion.
